text: So. The Combine's auditor. Imara Osei; I have had this station eleven years. Sit, if you can find a chair that is not full of requisition forms.
I will save you some time. Comms have been down eight months. The supply drone is three months overdue. My reactor is older than my chief engineer and my water plant is held together with hope.
And yet nobody here has died of anything but old age in six years. I would like you to see how that is done before you write a word. Will you do that?

choices.text: That is what I am here for. Show me.
I will go where the evidence goes, Administrator.
From what you describe, I could write the report now.

briefing_cold.text: You could. You would be wrong, and ten people would lose the only home most of them have. Look first. Please.

text: I am giving you the run of the control boards: any system console will answer to you. Use that carefully. People here are proud of what they keep alive.

Start with <y>Chief Kowal</y> in Engineering, west off the Ring. Then <y>Wren Castellanos</y> in Hydroponics, and <y>Dr. Pell</y> in the Medbay. Come back when you have seen all three and tell me what you think we are.

findings.text: You have been round all three. Well? Not the report. Just what you saw.

choices.text: People holding a wreck together with their bare hands. I can work with that.
A station one failure away from a funeral.
I saw a research lab drawing more power than your food supply.

findings_lab.text: ...Dr. Suvari's allocation. Yes. I signed that. I had reasons, and I am not ready to give them to the Combine's auditor. You have authority over the boards; I will not stop you using it.

text: The tug comes back on <y>Day 6 at 08:00</y>. Until then the station is what it is, and what you help it be.
If something is broken and you can mend it, mend it. If somebody is in your way, come to me. My door is the only one on this deck that does not lock.

variants.text: The tank gauge is in the red. I have rationed before; I can do it again. What do you need?
Kowal tells me the reactor is on its knees. Tell me you have better news.
Come in. You are the first auditor I have not wanted to put out of an airlock.
Auditor. What can I do for you?

choices.text: Where does my report stand, in your view?
The amplifier core. Who should have it?
choices.if: flag('knows_amp') and not flag('amp_released') and not flag('amp_taken')

choices.text: What is under the dig, Administrator?

choices.if: flag('knows_dex_scheme') and not flag('dex_exposed') and not flag('dex_reformed') and present('dex')

choices.text: I need the stores opened to engineering.
Is there a way for this station to refuse the Combine?

variants.text: Look at the boards. Reactor steady, tanks holding. That is a viable station, and you helped make it one. Write that.

Reactor at {round(cond('reactor'))} percent. Tanks at {round(res_pct('water'))}. I will not insult you by calling that healthy. But it can be mended, and you have {max(0, round(hours_until(6, 8)))} hours.

text: Kowal has not taken a rest day in two years. Wren could get work on any station in the Belt and stays here. Pell is paying off a debt that was cleared in his third year; I have never told him.
Halloran thinks he is guarding me. Pip thinks we are one repair from rescue. Lin... Lin is brilliant and I am afraid of what that is costing her.
And Dex gets us things nobody else could get, and I have chosen not to ask how. That may have been a mistake.
One core. Pip would give us a voice again. Lin would give us... an answer, she says. I locked it away because I could not choose, and not choosing was easier.
You are the outsider. You choose. Tell Halloran I said to release it to you - and then live with it, as I would have had to.
Eight months ago Tuck's bore broke into a void that is not on any survey. There is a made thing in it. It was transmitting before we arrived and it changed when we did.
I kept it out of the logs. If the Combine knew, they would strip this moon to the bedrock and us with it. So I told myself I was protecting my people. I am no longer sure who I was protecting.

choices.text: You did what you thought would keep them alive.
You falsified station records. That goes in the report.

signal_who.text: Lin, Tuck, me. Halloran suspects. And now a Combine auditor. So the question is not what is under the ice. The question is what you are going to do about it.

dex.text: I know what Dex is. Do you have proof, or a feeling? Halloran can act on proof. If you only have a feeling, I suggest you talk to Dex yourself; he is at his most honest when he thinks he is making a deal.

stores.text: Dex will scream. Let him. As of now engineering draws parts and scrap from the stores without his countersignature. I should have done it a year ago.
do: log('The Administrator opened the hardware stores to engineering.')

text: Refuse them. ...There is one way. The founding charter, Clause Nine: a resident crew may refuse decommissioning if the station sustains itself. Nobody has dared in forty years.

It would need the crew behind it. All of them, or near enough. And a station that can truly stand alone. Take the charter from my records shelf. If you mean to try, you will need to wave it under that captain's nose.

final_day.text: They are here. Whatever you say at that airlock, say it knowing all ten of us will be listening. Go.
